intro: A water spirit sings beneath a tremble of piano chords in Ondine, the first of Ravel’s three poems for piano. Andriy Makarevych plays the song and the water with the same two hands.

sections.label: A · A song beneath trembling chords
sections.mNote: The left hand sings below the repeated treble chords

sections.label: B · Arpeggios across the keyboard
sections.mNote: The water figures stretch further between bass and treble

sections.label: Dev · The song amid breaking waves
sections.mNote: Large arpeggios surround the melody in chords

sections.label: C · The waves subside
sections.mNote: Quieter arpeggios surround the returning song

sections.label: Link · A voice without accompaniment
sections.mNote: Très lent: the water figures stop

sections.label: Coda · A rush of notes, then C♯
sections.mNote: Rapid scales settle into quiet C♯-major arpeggios

cues.title: A song under water
cues.text: The right hand trembles on closely packed chords, ppp. Below them the left hand sings a slower line, marked very soft and very expressive. The melody sits inside the water, several notes below the glittering top of the piano.
cues.evidence: Durand score (1909), plate D. & F. 7207, p. 3: Lent, ppp right-hand chords and très doux et très expressif melody. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/6/6a/IMSLP246875-PMLP02576-Ravel,_Maurice-Gaspard_de_la_nuit_Durand_7207_scan.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: A palace beneath the lake
cues.text: In Bertrand’s poem, Ondine touches a moonlit window and offers the man inside her ring. “Mon palais est bâti fluide, au fond du lac” — “My palace is built of water, at the bottom of the lake.” She wants him to marry her and become king of the lakes.
cues.evidence: Aloysius Bertrand, Ondine, reproduced before the movement in Durand’s Gaspard de la nuit (1909), from the Mercure de France edition of 1908. Second and fourth paragraphs; our translation.

cues.title: The keyboard opens wide
cues.text: The arpeggios sweep from deep bass to high treble. Ravel sets the tune in chords among them, with swells from pp to forte inside a single wave. The pianist has to make those longer notes sing through the spray.
cues.evidence: Durand score, pp. 9–11: wide arpeggios, chordal melody and repeated crescendo hairpins.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: He loves a mortal woman
cues.text: Ondine’s invitation fails. The man tells her that he loves a mortal woman. Bertrand’s water spirit sheds a few tears, bursts out laughing and vanishes in a shower down the blue windowpanes.
cues.evidence: Bertrand, Ondine, final paragraph, printed before the movement in the Durand score (1909).

cues.title: The water falls silent
cues.text: Near the end, the accompaniment stops. A single line speaks in the middle of the keyboard, Très lent, with rests below it. For a few bars the song has no water around it.
cues.evidence: Durand score, p. 13, final system: unaccompanied Très lent phrase.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Laughter and a shower
cues.text: A two-handed rush breaks out, Rapide et brillant, then dissolves into quiet C♯-major arpeggios. Bertrand’s last image is “mes vitraux bleus” — “my blue stained-glass windows” — with water streaming down them.
cues.evidence: Durand score, p. 14: Rapide et brillant, retenez peu à peu, ppp and return to C♯ major. Quotation from Bertrand’s Ondine, final paragraph, printed before the music in the 1909 edition; our translation.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

transitions.title: The song loses its accompaniment
transitions.how: The piano’s running figures climb to a held high note and stop under a fermata. Ravel then writes Très lent. A quiet, unaccompanied phrase follows in the middle of the keyboard; the bass staff is empty.
transitions.evidence: Durand score (1909), p. 13, final system: fermata, followed by the unaccompanied Très lent line.

transitions.title: A rush across both hands
transitions.to: Coda · A rush of notes, then C♯
transitions.how: The bare phrase launches a rush of notes in both hands, marked Rapide et brillant. Ravel then asks the pianist to hold back gradually. C♯-major arpeggios return at ppp, in the opening tempo, and carry the music to its last quiet chord.
transitions.evidence: Durand score, p. 14: Rapide et brillant, retenez peu à peu, au mouvement du début and final C♯-major arpeggios.

composer.epithet: He made a ballet from two tunes and a snare drum, and gave his war dead a suite of dances.
facts: Paris Conservatoire from 1889; Fauré for composition, André Gedalge for counterpoint
Ricardo Viñes · Maurice Delage · Tristan Klingsor · M. D. Calvocoressi
Le Belvédère, Montfort-l’Amaury, 1921–37; now a museum
Two operas, two piano concertos, ballets, songs, chamber and piano music; no symphony

quote.text: Does it never occur to these people that I may be artificial by nature?
quote.source: To M. D. Calvocoressi, recalled in his Musicians Gallery (1933)

composer.background:
Ravel’s father took his sons to factories to see the machinery. His mother sang to them. Pierre-Joseph was a Swiss-born engineer; Marie Delouart was Basque and had grown up in Madrid. Maurice was born in Ciboure on 7 March 1875, and the family moved to Paris three months later. He kept returning to the Basque coast, and Spain kept returning in his music: the plucked-guitar attacks of Alborada del gracioso, the habanera that rocks through the Rapsodie espagnole, the clocks ticking in a Toledo shop in L’heure espagnole.

He entered the Paris Conservatoire at fourteen, studied piano with Charles-Wilfrid de Bériot and lost his place in 1895 for failing to win the required prizes. Two teachers then understood him: André Gedalge, who gave him counterpoint lessons from 1897, and Fauré, whose composition class he entered in January 1898. Ricardo Viñes, his friend since adolescence, became the pianist his music needed. Viñes gave the first performances of Jeux d’eau, Miroirs and Gaspard de la nuit, pieces their composer could never have played with comparable command.
